chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Barqi, from Asram ibn Hawshab, from Isa ibn Abdillah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said:
The valleys of the Sanctuary (al-Haram) flow in the open land (al-Hill), and the valleys of the open land do not flow in the Sanctuary.

key_terms.أَوْدِيَةُ: Valleys or wadis, referring to the dry riverbeds or valleys in the region.
key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Sanctuary (specifically Mecca), a sacred area where certain actions are restricted for pilgrims.
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: The open land or non-sanctuary area surrounding the Haram.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in water flow between the valleys of the Haram and the Hill?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the hydrological and legal boundaries of the Haram, establishing that the sanctity of the inner sanctuary does not extend to the water flow originating from outside, nor does the open land's flow penetrate the sacred zone. This natural demarcation serves as a practical criterion for determining the limits of ritual restrictions (such as hunting prohibitions) for the Muhrim, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on observable natural signs in deriving fiqh. It highlights the precision with which the Imams defined the spatial extent of the Haram to ensure pilgrims could accurately observe their duties.
